original.reason: For real (or complex) sequences, convergence implies the Cauchy property; the reverse triangle inequality makes the absolute-value sequence Cauchy, hence convergent by completeness.

judgment.reason: Correct Cauchy-sequence proof using the reverse triangle inequality and completeness.
Directly proves that |s_n| converges to |s| via the reverse triangle inequality.
Correctly applies continuity of the absolute-value function to a convergent sequence.
A complete direct proof that t_n=|s_n| converges to |s|.
